attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel shows each signer's full name and postal code, not the agreed first name, last initial and city. Confirmed signers' personal data is published on every petition page as soon as the flag reaches 10%.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: The organizer-news consent is pre-ticked and bundles unrelated campaigns, so it is not a freely given, specific, opt-in consent under GDPR for EU signers. Organizers would then send marketing to EU signers who never actively agreed.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked> ... Keep me updated about this campaign and others from {{ petition.organizer.name }}

attacks.claim: The 409 response for a duplicate email lets anyone submit an address and learn whether it has signed a specific petition. That exposes political-opinion linkage for the signer without their knowledge.
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409

attacks.claim: EU residency is chosen by postal code, with everything else defaulting to us-east-1. Signers whose postal code does not resolve, or who are EU residents with non-EU codes, have their data stored in the US with no stated transfer mechanism for that case.
attacks.evidence: Postgres, eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise

attacks.claim: Validation errors are shown only by a red border and background. No text message is ever written to the aria-live paragraph, and no aria-invalid or per-field error text is set, so screen-reader users get no explanation of what failed (WCAG 3.3.1, 1.4.1).
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

attacks.claim: Only 422 and success are handled. A 409 duplicate, a 5xx, or a network failure produces no feedback and leaves the button active, so signers do not know whether their signature counted and may retry.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) { ... } if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: The axe-core scan covers only the default sign page. It does not test error states, the focus move, or the live-region announcement, so the 0-violation result does not support the accessibility claim for the flows that fail.
attacks.evidence: axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations

attacks.claim: The QA table reports the Recent signers panel as Pass, but that test did not check the agreed name-masking rule, and the template violates it. The QA result is contradicted by the artifact's own template.
attacks.evidence: Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed | Pass

attacks.claim: The client sets window.location from a server Location header without checking it. This is low risk only if the server guarantees a same-origin path, which the artifact does not state.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: All confirmation emails, including those for EU signers, go through a single US-based vendor. The artifact cites a DPA but not the transfer mechanism or an exit path.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14

attacks.claim: There is no fetch timeout or retry, and no alert covers 409 or network-error rates. The watched sign_submit_error_rate metric may not capture these failures.
attacks.evidence: Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: Live polling every 15s plus a recent_signers query on each page view was not part of the 400/s load test, so its load at launch traffic is unmeasured.
attacks.evidence: Signature counts update live (polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s)

attacks.claim: Rollback flips the flag but does not un-publish signer names already shown or recall confirmation emails already sent. The rollout also targets petition pages rather than users, which is not stated as a design choice.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: Some US states have their own petition-signing rules, such as required fields or signer-verification standards. The artifact does not mention checking these.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no review of state-level petition law
